event.hall_dance.11.text: The ladder can wait one night. One dance. I built this floor to take it.
event.hall_dance.11.why: answers Tilda's ladder coin instead of ignoring it; drops a second 'twice' after .0

event.marcus_heart8.intro.text: Come in. You've seen the barn I carved at nine. Now see the roof plan. Not many have.
event.marcus_heart8.intro.why: remembers heart 5's carving (gated on it); frees the measuring for r0

dlg.marcus.roof.r2.text: The ladder. Plain, steady, necessary. Best offer anyone's made that roof.
dlg.marcus.roof.r2.why: n1 already says six winters; no repeat in one scene

event.story_pumpkin_marcus.intro.text: You've caught me. A practice lantern. I measured the face. I never asked whose pumpkin.
event.story_pumpkin_marcus.intro.why: no longer the same 'Ah. You've found' opener as the whistler scene; drops a 'twice'

dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.0.text: Tilda comes around the corner, stops, and stares at the pumpkin's new face.
dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.0.why: narration now brings Tilda in before she speaks instead of re-setting the scene after Marcus's line

event.story_pumpkin_marcus.after.text: It goes back with a face carved in. Tilda calls it an improvement. Next year, I ask first. Probably.
event.story_pumpkin_marcus.after.why: ends on a promise with a hedge instead of a closed smile

dlg.story.whistler.marcus.r0.text: Hello. Yes. Hello. A normal approach. It's rarer than you'd think.
dlg.story.whistler.marcus.r0.why: trims one of too many 'thank you' openers

dlg.marcus.birthday.r0.text: Thank you. I'll write that on the beam, small, where only I'll look.
dlg.marcus.birthday.r0.why: the tic was wallpaper; still sets up the after-branch's beam

dlg.marcus.birthday.r1.text: Oak. Straight grain, no knots. Most people see a board. You saw the grain.
dlg.marcus.birthday.r1.why: second 'thank you' in the scene cut; truest word last

event.overheard_bram_marcus_2.l2.text: Made you one. Oak. Measured your grip while you weren't looking.

event.overheard_bram_marcus_3.l2.text: A hundred and four. All straight. I counted.
event.overheard_bram_marcus_3.l2.why: one fewer 'twice'; keeps Bram's 'more' reply working

threads.marcus_heart2: None of the leftover wood is long enough for the hall roof, and he checked: what does the roof need?
threads.marcus_heart5: Edmund's cellar door, the one he would not let Marcus oil.
threads.hall_dance: The roof is finally finished; the lamps burn low and nobody goes home.
threads.story_pie_payoff: Two bakers are now baking again; the pie feud is not over.
threads.story_whistler_marcus: Wednesdays on the bench, Marcus whistles and Bram pretends not to hear: go and listen.
threads.story_pumpkin_marcus: Next year he will ask first. Probably.
threads.marcus_heart8: The roof plan: measured, redrawn, or still nearly fixed, depending on the choice.
threads.marcus_birthday: The beam, or the plank over the door, that will outlast them both.
threads.overheard_marcus_odalys_3: Marcus is building Dr. Penn a chair for her Saturdays.

notes: story_pumpkin_marcus: Tilda speaks (n1, r0, r2) but is not placed in the scene; she needs a place/walk-in beat before n1. I rewrote n0 narration to bring her round the corner.
story_pumpkin_marcus: old n0 narration said 'Behind the store', but the scene uses the same Village tile (25,18) as the whistler and pie scenes; my new narration drops the location.

Variety pass: 'measure twice' was in 13 lines; cut to the signature beats (heart2, hall_dance.0, heart8 r0/after, Odalys 1 where her reply depends on it, Dorian window). R1 notes naming me (six winters, two-people dance, Saturdays) are already applied on the cards.
